page: Microsoft Azure HB368-144rs_v5 is a high-performance computing virtual machine instance provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V. Built on the x86_64 architecture with Intel processors, the instance allocates 144 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading. Memory resources total 448.0 GB of RAM, providing an allocation ratio of 3.11 GB per core. The instance includes support for RDMA networking and Premium Storage integration.

Storage configuration features 15,875 GB of local NVMe solid-state storage directly attached to the host, facilitating high throughput and low-latency disk operations. No graphics processing units are included in this deployment. The combination of high core counts, dedicated resource allocation, and large NVMe disk arrays yields dense compute and high input/output processing capacity.

Cost efficiency is driven by the density of dedicated compute cores and bundled local storage, reducing the need for secondary local storage attachments in high-throughput workflows. Tradeoffs involve the lack of hardware accelerators such as GPUs and an allocation of memory per core that sits around 3.11 GB, which is tuned specifically for compute-bound scaling rather than extreme in-memory databases.

Workloads suited for Microsoft Azure HB368-144rs_v5 include high-performance computing, computational fluid dynamics, finite element analysis, weather simulation, molecular modeling, large-scale compilation jobs, and data-intensive batch processing pipelines relying on rapid local NVMe scratch space.
